function: Beam tracking for a BS-to-UAV link: an LSTM predicts the UAV position and a generative diffusion model selects beam direction, beam width and number of antennas (p. 5-8).
system: BS square UPA, 16-128 antennas per side, one RF chain; LoS mmWave link to a UAV with one antenna array; no RIS; frequency not stated (p. 3, 7, 11).
method: Two-layer LSTM (64 units, RMSE loss, backpropagation) predicts positions; Q-network-guided generative diffusion model (5 denoising steps) designs beams; supervised plus RL-style training (p. 6-9, 11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS Friis path loss with UPA array response; UAV 3-D trajectories from dynamic model [42] with wind noise; no standard channel model or measured data (p. 4, 10).
test_conditions: LSTM trained online on past UAV positions (L=15); evaluated at 10 and 50 m/s, with 10 m/s wind and S-bend path; no separate training condition stated (p. 7, 12-13).
baselines: Non-learned: traditional phased-array beam tracking, Kalman filter. Learned: GPR angle-prediction beam tracking [30], AGAIN-based beam tracking [47]; LSTM compared with GPR and KF (p. 11-13).
metrics: Communication interruption rate, number of beam switches, SNR and relative error, energy efficiency, cosine similarity of prediction, antenna saving, fitting time (p. 11-13).
complexity: Order O(Niter x NL x (Nd x Nalig x N)) stated; measured time per operation cycle versus baselines in Fig. 14(b) (p. 10, 13).
q1_support: p. 4: "the channel adopts the Friis transmission model to describe the signal fading between the BS and UAV"; custom LoS simulator, trajectories from a dynamic model (p. 10); no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 7: "The historical motion features of UAV and updated motion features are iteratively used to optimize the model parameters"; speeds, wind and S-bend path are evaluation scenarios, but the paper never states a training condition different from the test condition.
q3_support: p. 13: "compared to the AGAIN method, the PPBT-AR algorithm achieves a lower number of beam switches"; non-learned baseline, p. 13: "compared to the traditional phased array beam tracking algorithm, PPBT-AR reduces the number of beam switches"
q4_support: p. 10: "the overall complexity of the proposed PPBT-AR algorithm can be expressed as" O(Niter x NL x (Nd x Nalig x N)); p. 13: "its time consumption remains comparable to that of the AGAIN algorithm"
q5_support: p. 10: "the 3-D flight trajectory of the UAV relative to the BS is generated by the dynamic model mentioned in [42]"; no code or data link and no public dataset is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 6 chosen because the learned beam control serves a BS-to-UAV aerial link and the tie-break puts 6 before 3; area 3 (BS beamforming) is the alternative. The UAV trajectory is predicted, not controlled, so above_phy does not apply. q3 rests on GPR beam tracking [30] and the AGAIN-based tracker [47] (action space, p. 10) as learned baselines, and on phased-array tracking as the non-learned one. q2 is 0 because the speed, wind and S-bend scenarios are separate evaluations of an online-updated LSTM (p. 7, 12-13).
